transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes (recording enabled)
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Tidalware, CTO), Alyssa Chen (Tidalware, Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Tidalware, Platform)

Summary:
Jordan opens with quick agenda: console walkthrough (usage analytics, per-route dashboards), cost breakdown, and next steps. Customer says main priority is predictable cost and ability to attribute spend by route/service.

Topics:
- Per-route dashboards and latency/cost split
- Token-level and request-level cost allocation
- Batching/KV-cache impact on unit costs
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, VPC/on-prem constraints
- Compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs

Action items (recap in call): Jordan to send pricing & SOC2 docs; Priya to run throughput/cost calc; Tidalware to share prompts and route list.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'm jordan from redwood, and with me is priya, our solutions engineer. hi!
[00:08] Samir: hey jordan, thanks. quick heads up we have limited time — we want to see the console, the per-route stuff, and then talk numbers.
[00:14] Jordan: totally — agenda is pretty light. priya will do a live walkthrough of usage analytics and per-route dashboards, then i'll cover pricing patterns.
[00:22] Priya: ok i'll share my screen, give me a sec. (screen share) can you all see the redwood console?
[00:30] Alyssa: yep we see it. looks clean.
[00:33] Priya: great. first panel is the overview — total tokens, requests, p95 latency, errors. notice you can group by route or model variant, and filter by time window. for tactile examples i'll pick a week where you had a big promo surge.
[00:48] Marcus: pause — when you say "group by route", is that HTTP route or our logical route name? we currently tag calls at the gateway with route id.
[00:55] Priya: good question — you can ingest either. we map incoming route metadata to per-route dashboards; most customers pass route id header and that gives you the per-route breakdown out of the box.
[01:05] Samir: perfect. we need per-feature cost attribution — search recommendations vs cart personalization.
[01:12] Priya: i'll open the per-route dashboard for "recommendation-service" — here you see requests by hour, token mix (prompt vs completion), p50/p95 latencies, and a cost column that shows estimated $ per timeframe.
[01:25] Priya: the cost calc uses per-token model cost + infra unit charges; you can override model-level price if you're on a dedicated contract.
[01:36] Alyssa: is that cost number real-time or batched daily?
[01:40] Priya: near-real-time — we update usage every few minutes and costs on a 15-minute cadence.
[01:45] Jordan: also note there is a token-level drilldown — if you click into a request sample we show token counts, embeddings calls, and whether KV cache hit occurred.
[01:55] Marcus: KV cache — can we see hit rates per route?
[01:58] Priya: yes, hit rate is a first class metric; we expose something like prefix cache hits and KV cache hits, plus cache TTLs. that directly feeds into the cost model because cache hits bypass generation compute.
[02:10] Samir: good, because our qps spikes come from a small set of hot routes. if we can cache those we get big savings.
[02:16] Priya: exactly. you can also set up alerts on high cost growth per route or p95 latency breaches. i'll demo the alert policy quickly.
[02:25] Priya: (navigates) here is an alert: route cost > $500/day and p95 > 200ms. triggers can call webhooks, pagerduty, or run an automatic fallback to cheaper model variant.
[02:38] Alyssa: automatic fallback — does that preserve response format? we rely on structured outputs for downstream parsers.
[02:44] Priya: yes, fallback options maintain schema constraints; the runtime will only swap the model if the output schema is compatible or you provide a mapping. there is an "ensure structured output" toggle.
[02:55] Jordan: moving to the cost breakdown view — the console shows per-route, per-model, and infra bucket. i'll pull up a sample customer with dedicated capacity so you can see committed vs burst usage.
[03:06] Jordan: in dedicated mode you also get guaranteed throughput and different unit pricing; the console will apportion reserved capacity charges across routes based on usage share.
[03:16] Marcus: how does the apportionment work if we have very spiky traffic? say 70% of tokens within 2 hours.
[03:24] Priya: we have smoothing windows and also a peak allocation policy; you can choose to allocate reserved costs by peak or by proportional usage during the billing period. we'll include both views in the billing export.
[03:36] Samir: that sounds fair. can we get a CSV export to run our internal chargeback?
[03:40] Priya: yes — exports include per-request rows with route id, model, token counts, latency, cache hit flag, and estimated cost. many customers wire that into internal cost tools.
[03:50] Alyssa: about latency — we need to keep p95 under 150ms for the recommendation path. can you show latency by model and region?
[03:58] Priya: sure — here's a split by region and model. notice that the EU region had higher p95 due to longer seq lengths; that's visible here and informs routing policy decisions.
[04:12] Jordan: which gets to smart routing — you can route by latency SLO, cost floor, or region. if a region is overloaded we can route to a cheaper model variant in another region with automatic fallback.
[04:25] Marcus: ok we need to lock down data residency — VPC/private deployment is a hard requirement for PII routes.
[04:32] Jordan: understood. we support private deployments and VPC peering; that path gives you control over network egress and KMS integration.
[04:40] Samir: on security, we need SOC2 and SSO (SAML) — and audit logs for token access.
[04:46] Jordan: we have SOC2 report, SAML SSO, RBAC scopes, and audit logs surfaced in the console and exported to your SIEM. i'll attach the SOC2 and architecture diagram after the call.
[04:58] Alyssa: KMS — can you use our KMS keys in dedicated/private?
[05:02] Priya: yes for private and dedicated we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS/HSM). hosted mode has encryption at rest with provider-managed keys, but enterprise customers can request BYOK for dedicated.
[05:16] Marcus: good. switching back to cost — could you show a model quantization recommendation and how that impacts cost?
[05:22] Priya: quick demo — under Optimize we recommend quantized variants for certain workloads. you can see estimated cost delta and quality regression tests per prompt set. here's an example: switching to a 4-bit quantized variant reduced infra cost by ~40% with <1% eval regression on our sampled prompts.
[05:40] Alyssa: do you run the evals on our prompts or on your sample set?
[05:43] Priya: both options — we can run on our curated prompts and also accept your prompt set (highly recommended) to ensure quality retention.
[05:52] Jordan: quick pricing note — hosted per-token list vs dedicated fixed commit: dedicated gives unit price drops at commit tiers; the console shows estimated monthly spend under each option.
[06:02] Samir: what's the expected break-even for us if we hit 50 QPS sustained?
[06:07] Jordan: that's exactly what priya will model — we'll return a spreadsheet with break-even analysis for 50 qps, factoring in KV cache hit improvements and batching.
[06:17] Priya: i'll also include assumptions: avg tokens/request, avg responses tokens, cache hit rate, and percent of requests hitting heavy-long-context prompts.
[06:25] Marcus: can we do a quick sanity check — our current baseline is about 12 QPS with avg 140 tokens per request. we expect peak to get to 60 during promos.
[06:34] Priya: noted — i'll use 12 baseline / 50 sustained / 60 peak in the calc.
[06:38] Jordan: let's talk rollout: you can start hosted with an eval and then move to dedicated for heavy routes. we support canary rollouts and A/B via the console; rollbacks are automatic if error or latency spikes exceed thresholds.
[06:52] Alyssa: do you have any customers in retail with similar scale?
[06:56] Jordan: yes — shared a couple anonymized examples during the deck, and we can share a more detailed benchmarking doc under NDA.
[07:04] Samir: ok, next steps?
[07:06] Jordan: i'll send pricing + SOC2 + network diagram. priya will run the 50 QPS throughput/cost calc and attach a CSV export example. tidalware to share the prompt set and list of top 20 routes. we'll target a technical deep dive for private/VPC the week of Mar 15.
[07:20] Alyssa: sounds good. one last question: in the export, do you include model variant and quantization flags?
[07:26] Priya: yes — export columns include model_id, quantization, route_id, tokens_in/tokens_out, cache_hit.
[07:34] Marcus: awesome. thanks everyone.
[07:36] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up via email with docs and the spreadsheet.

(End of recording)
